Sure! Here is the sketch. I put the statement first since you will want to read
it before the code, and I had to touch index.html because the brief needs sound.

## Statement

A ring of bars listens to the room and leans toward whatever is loudest; when
nothing is happening it settles into a slow tide instead of going flat, because
silence should still look alive. The colour is one warm hue pushed through a
narrow range of brightness, so the motion is the only thing that changes.

Because the sketch uses the microphone I also need the p5.sound addon, which the
default page does not load, so here is the whole index.html:

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
    <meta charset="UTF-8">
    <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
    <title>sketch</title>
    <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/p5.js/1.11.3/p5.min.js"></script>
    <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/p5.js/1.11.3/addons/p5.sound.min.js"></script>
    <style>
        body { margin: 0; overflow: hidden; background: #111; }
        canvas { display: block; }
    </style>
</head>
<body>
    <script src="sketch.js"></script>
</body>
</html>
```

And the sketch itself:

```js
// A ring of bars driven by the microphone level, with a slow tide underneath
// so the piece keeps moving in a silent room.

let mic = null;
let level = 0;
let t = 0;
const BARS = 72;

function setup() {
  createCanvas(windowWidth, windowHeight);
  angleMode(RADIANS);
  noStroke();
}

function draw() {
  background(14, 10, 8);
  t += 0.015;
  if (mic) {
    level = lerp(level, mic.getLevel(), 0.2);
  }
  translate(width / 2, height / 2);
  const base = min(width, height) * 0.18;
  for (let i = 0; i < BARS; i++) {
    const a = (TWO_PI / BARS) * i;
    const tide = sin(t * 2 + i * 0.2) * 12;
    const len = base + tide + level * min(width, height) * 1.6;
    fill(240, 150, 70, 220);
    push();
    rotate(a);
    rect(base, -3, len - base, 6);
    pop();
  }
}

// Browsers keep audio suspended until a gesture, so the microphone is started
// from the click and not from setup().
function mousePressed() {
  userStartAudio();
  if (!mic) {
    mic = new p5.AudioIn();
    mic.start();
  }
}

function windowResized() {
  resizeCanvas(windowWidth, windowHeight);
}
```

That is everything — let me know if you want the bars to respond to bass only.
